title: Invocation plumbing: parallel-safe tool injection and streaming stability
author: Sofia Patel
release_notes: Improves tool-calling ergonomics: safer parallel tool injections, incremental streaming of tool outputs into response stream, idempotent retry metadata, and OpenAI-compatible function_call adjustments. No public API breaking changes.
description:
Motivation: Users are leveraging multi-tool workflows with parallel tool invocations and streaming responses. We observed two classes of failures: 1) interleaved streaming + tool-injection races that produced malformed structured output, and 2) retry-induced duplicate injections when a tool run finished after a transient worker restart. This PR introduces end-to-end plumbing to make parallel tool calls safe, deterministic in the output stream, and compatible with OpenAI-style function_call ergonomics. Summary of changes: (a) Introduce an invocation coordinator component that assigns a short-lived invocation id and an idempotency token per tool call; (b) Implement a streaming injection buffer that serializes injections at token boundaries while preserving interleaved partial streams from model and tools; (c) Add a retry policy that consults the coordinator state and stashed artifact store to avoid duplicate injections; (d) Update the OpenAI compatibility layer to prefer "function_call" routing when structured output is requested, and to emit consistent function metadata in the streaming prelude. Design notes: The coordinator is a lightweight in-memory state machine in the runtime path with a pluggable backing (in-memory by default, Redis in Dedicated/Private). Each tool call is registered with metadata: invocation_id, tool_name, call_index, idempotency_token. Tool responses are written to a per-invocation buffer. For streaming, we produce three kinds of stream events: MODEL_CHUNK, TOOL_PRELUDE, TOOL_CHUNK. TOOL_PRELUDE contains structured meta (tool id, sequence id, final=true/false) so consumers can reconstruct structured output even if chunks are interleaved. To keep latency low we allow optimistic pass-through of MODEL_CHUNK while the coordinator reserves insertion points for TOOL_PRELUDE; if a tool arrives late the coordinator injects a placeholder and then patches with TOOL_CHUNK(s) when available. Retry and duplicate-suppression: retry attempts include the idempotency_token; the coordinator keeps a short-lived cache (TTL 5 minutes) of completed tool results and will return the cached artifact instead of re-invoking the tool. For failed in-progress runs we allow best-effort cancellation and a clean fallback marker in the stream so downstream can detect and request re-run if desired. OpenAI compatibility tweaks: when a client requests the OpenAI "function_call" flow, we automatically translate tool metadata into function descriptors and emit an initial streaming message that matches function call prelude semantics. This preserves compatibility with existing SDKs and reduces lifting for customers migrating from OpenAI APIs. Testing and validation: unit tests for coordinator state transitions, integration tests for parallel tool runs (2-6 concurrent tools), a fuzz test that interleaves model and tool chunks at high frequency, and an end-to-end scenario that verifies deterministic structured output assembly under flaky RPCs. Performance: the coordinator adds ~0.4ms median overhead per invocation in our microbenchmarks; batching unchanged for model tokens. Rollout plan: feature gated by runtime flag and behind an opt-in in Console for first 2 weeks, then gradual rollout to 25% of hosted traffic for validation. Checklist: - [x] Coordinator state machine implementation - [x] Streaming injection buffer - [x] Idempotency token and artifact cache - [x] OpenAI compatibility mapping - [x] Unit and integration tests - [x] Documentation snippets (Console + SDKs) - [x] Feature flag + rollout plan

Editors note: kept the description compact; detailed design doc attached in repo docs folder.

review_conversation: Marcus Chen: Overall looks good. Two questions: how does the coordinator behave under clock skew across nodes?

Sofia Patel: We keep coordinator per-host by default; for Dedicated/Private we recommend Redis backing which uses logical timestamps. I added tests that simulate small skews and ensure idempotency is not violated.
Elena Gomez: The placeholder + patching behavior could confuse existing consumers expecting strict streaming shape. Can we include a debug flag to emit explicit PATCH events?
Sofia Patel: Yes — added optional PATCH frames for early adopters; default remains placeholder->chunk to minimize protocol churn. Documentation updated to call this out.
Priya Nair: CI flaky on the fuzz test earlier; looked like a teardown race. Fixed by extending teardown wait and stubbing a delayed RPC path.
Reviewer Bot: Integration tests passed on re-run, no new flaky markers.
Team Lead (Carlos Vega): Approving after the Redis-backed coordinator doc is added and a short incident runbook is included.
Sofia Patel: Addressed feedback, added runbook and a small migration note for Dedicated customers. Ready to merge.
merge_outcome: Merged by squash on 2026-03-02 by Carlos Vega. Commit message: feat(runtime): safe parallel tool invocation + streaming injection (ENG-12940, ENG-12822).
notes_for_release: Enable feature flag by default on hosted after 2-week opt-in window. Monitor metrics: tool_injection_latencies, tool_dup_suppressed, stream_patch_rate. Notify Dedicated customers about optional Redis backing for stronger cross-node guarantees.
public_impact_summary: No immediate breaking API changes. OpenAI compatibility improved so existing function_call clients should see more deterministic streaming. SDK updates include small ergonomic helpers for idempotency; see SDK release notes for migration steps.
